title: Implement policy flattening for RBACv2 and audit metadata normalizer
author: Evelyn Cho
description:
Context and motivation: RBACv2 policy evaluation has seen increased PDP (policy decision point) CPU and cache churn on high-cardinality operator bindings. At the same time audit ingestion carries a lot of redundant metadata keys from different parts of the stack which makes downstream analytics noisy and expensive. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) a policy-flattening pass in the RBACv2 compilation pipeline that materializes nested role conditions into a compact flattened decision trie to reduce runtime branching and memory allocations; 2) an audit metadata normalizer that canonicalizes common header keys, trims excessive claim payloads, and adds a provenance fingerprint for de-dup and sampling.

What this change does (high level):
- RBAC: new compiler stage rbac/flatten_pass.go that converts nested policy expressions into a normalized flat set of rules with stable ordering, and emits a compact binary decision trie used by the PDP runtime. This reduces per-decision heap allocations and improves CPU cache locality.
- Audit: new service audit/normalizer/service.go that rewrites noisy keys (e.g., multi-named tenant identifiers, legacy region tags) into canonical fields and computes a content-hash provenance header (X-Audit-Proof) to help ingestion dedup and sampling.
- Runtime: small PDP runtime change to accept flattened policy blobs and a graceful fallback to the old evaluator when incoming policy version is unknown.
- KMS/Residency: normalizer preserves region-pin metadata and ensures KMS key identifiers are passed through an allowlist; no changes to key-wrapping semantics.

Why this is safe:
- Backwards-compatible: the PDP supports both the new flattened format and the legacy AST-based evaluator. New policy bundles published by the compiler include a version header. No live policy is mutated in place.
- Tests: added unit and integration tests that exercise both evaluators and the normalizer. CI runs showed stable results after two reruns.

Checklist (PR scope):
- [x] Compiler flattening pass with tests
- [x] PDP runtime support and fallback
- [x] Audit normalizer + provenance header
- [x] Add allowlist for KMS identifiers and preserve region pins
- [x] End-to-end integration test with policy bundle rollout simulation
- [x] Documentation: rbac/README.md and audit/normalizer/README.md

Rollout plan:
1) Merge on main behind feature flag rbac.flattening.enabled=false by default.
2) Deploy compiler that emits flattened bundles to staging and push a small percentage of tenants (canary) to consume flattened bundles.
3) Gradually enable rbac.flattening.enabled=true for more tenants after verifying PDP latency and correctness.

Migration notes: policy authors do not need to change YAML. The compiler will emit both legacy and flattened artifacts for 2 release cycles. If any tenant relies on operator-ordered policy semantics we provide a compatibility shim via rbac.compatibility_mode in config.

Security and compliance considerations: normalizer strips non-essential personally-identifiable metadata from audit payloads unless explicitly whitelisted. The provenance fingerprint is derived from canonicalized fields and HMACed using a cluster-local signing key; the design was reviewed with Security and complies with our audit retention policy. KMS keys are forwarded only if present in the allowlist; disallowed KMS ids are logged and the request is routed to the origin-mode with an alert for manual review.

Performance results (staging canary):
- Median PDP decision latency: improved from 1.8ms -> 1.05ms (approx 42% improvement) under realistic operator binding load.
- GC/allocations: ~35% reduction in allocation bytes per decision.
- Audit ingestion size: ~12% reduction in average event size after normalization (depends on tenant).

Related work / references: ENG-7882 (policy compiler perf), ENG-7921 (audit ingestion noise reduction). Related PRs: reference to the policy linter PR will be added as a follow-up.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on correctness of the flattening transformation (rbac/flatten_pass.go) and on the normalizer whitelist logic. Tests include randomized property checks to ensure flattened rules and legacy evaluator agree for generated policy forests.

merge_outcome: Merged by Maya Singh via squash-merge on 2024-11-20. Merge commit message: 'Flatten RBAC policies and normalize audit metadata — improve PDP latency and reduce audit noise.'
release_notes: Introduce RBACv2 policy flattening compiler stage and audit metadata normalizer. Feature gated rollout; provides improved PDP latency and reduced audit ingestion noise. No user-facing YAML changes required. Enable via feature flag 'rbac.flattening.enabled'.
migration_instructions: Compiler will publish flattened bundles alongside legacy bundles for 2 releases. Operators should enable rbac.flattening.enabled in staging and monitor PDP latency and audit_normalizer.normalized_count metric. If incompatibility observed, set rbac.compatibility_mode=true to force legacy evaluator. Contact platform-eng for assisted rollouts.
security_review: Design reviewed by Security (Carlos Ruiz) on 2024-11-18. Normalizer HMAC provenance design approved; KMS forwarding uses allowlist checked in audit/normalizer/whitelist.go.
notes: This is intentionally staged; follow-up items: add policy linter guidance to reject constructs that expand badly when flattened, and a CLI tool to inspect flattened bundles for debugging.
